title: Skip the name you've heard twice
allegory: IOI is like a mail room where early clerks stamp the second 'John' as a repeat, couriers carry a 'John is taken' note to the front desk, and the front-desk clerks copy onto the reply whichever name is not on the note: Mary.
map: clerks who notice the second 'John' is a repeat
duplicate-token and induction heads acting at S2
couriers carrying a 'John is taken' note to the front desk
S-inhibition heads 7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10 moving the flag from S2 to END
front-desk clerks copying a name, skipping the one on the note
name movers 9.6, 9.9, 10.0 attending END to IO, with inhibition entering through their queries
a contrarian clerk who writes 'John' back in
how much more the reply favours Mary than John
logit difference logit[IO] − logit[S] at END

hamming.what: A one-template task, two names with one repeated, that GPT-2 small completes with the other name, reverse-engineered as 26 of its 144 heads in seven classes.
hamming.when: Whenever you need the reference example of finding, and proving, a circuit in a real pretrained model.
hamming.why: It set explicit standards (faithfulness, completeness, minimality) for when a mechanism story counts as found rather than merely fitting the plots.

object.title: The name relay
object.subtitle: GPT-2 small's IOI circuit as a relay: tokens along the floor, layers rising, the answer written at the top.

cap.1: 'When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to' ... Mary. Tokens line the floor; information climbs to the final 'to', where the answer goes.
cap.2: The IOI circuit laid out by position and depth: 26 heads in seven classes, ending in the logit difference at END.
cap.3: Wang et al. (2022): 26 of 144 heads, seven classes, validated causally against faithfulness, completeness and minimality.

cap.1: Early on, at the second John, a few heads notice it's a repeat of the first John.
cap.2: Duplicate-token and induction heads flag that S2 repeats S1.
cap.3: Previous-token and duplicate-token heads plus induction heads write a 'duplicated' signal into S2's residual stream.

cap.1: In the middle, couriers carry the note 'John is taken' across to the final word.
cap.2: S-inhibition heads 7.3, 7.9, 8.6 and 8.10 move that flag from S2 to END.
cap.3: S-inhibition heads V-compose with the duplicate signal: information is moved, not attention redirected. Activation patching shows their values matter and their keys mostly don't.

cap.1: At the top, name movers look back at the names and copy one. The note arrives in their question, so they skip John and copy Mary.
cap.2: Name movers 9.6, 9.9 and 10.0 attend from END to IO and copy it; the inhibition enters through their queries.
cap.3: The query route (not keys) is what path patching, rather than activation patching, is needed to establish.

cap.1: Two contrarian heads push John back up, and backup movers wait to take over if the main movers are knocked out.
cap.2: Head 10.7 alone makes the wrong answer about seven times more likely; backup movers mask single-head ablations.
cap.3: Negative movers 10.7 and 11.10 write against IO, with function unsettled; backup name movers make single-head ablation understate importance.

predict.q: You ablate name mover 9.9 and the logit difference barely drops. Why?

options.t: Backup name movers take over, so single-head ablation understates importance
9.9 was never part of the circuit

predict.why: Backup heads only step in once the primary movers are removed.

predict.q: To build a corrupted prompt for patching, which names should you flip?

options.t: Only the first S name, so token and position signals both flip

predict.why: Flipping all three reverses the token signal but leaves the position signal where it was, giving a murky mixed contrast.

predict.q: Why score with logit difference rather than the probability of ' Mary'?

options.t: It cancels shared preferences and is linear in the residual stream
It is always a bigger number

predict.why: Matched pairs and a signed difference remove biases such as the final layernorm's roughly one-logit tilt towards John.

object.where: Any circuit claim: a relay of parts you verify by intervening, judged on faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
